title: PHILGEPS + UNGM OPPORTUNITY BRIEFING

executive_summary.source_access_notes: PhilGEPS public notice recheck was partial: direct category-page fetches from the automation runtime looped redirects, so today’s PhilGEPS section is based on targeted official notice rechecks and tracked urgent items. UNGM public search and notice pages were scanned live.

best_opportunities.project: RFQ no. 2026-08-28-006_1 LOT_Procurement of Website Hosting and Technical Support Services for the Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (EPA) Digital Edition
best_opportunities.procuring_entity: Cultural Center of the Philippines - Pasay City Metro Manila
best_opportunities.procurement_method: Negotiated Procurement - Small Value Procurement (Sec. 34) / RFQ
best_opportunities.why_fit: This remains the cleanest near-term fit for AIStaff because it is service-led website hosting and technical support work under a small-value route, with a scope that can plausibly align with implementation, maintenance, integrations, and support rather than hardware resale.
important_requirements: Official public abstract previously verified on August 29, 2026 lists contract duration as 6 months
Public notice exposes a downloadable RFQ document link for the detailed scope

Post-award documents named in the abstract include signed quotation, valid Business/Mayor's Permit, PhilGEPS Registration, notarized Omnibus Sworn Statement with proof of authority if applicable, and latest 2025 annual income tax return plus business tax returns

Official contacts shown in the abstract: Regie Zapanta Profeta, regie.profeta@culturalcenter.gov.ph, plus submission contacts glycidas.penaranda@culturalcenter.gov.ph and pmd@culturalcenter.gov.ph, tel. 8551-0039
Public abstract does not clearly state the required PhilGEPS membership level or any prior-project threshold
risks_or_blockers: The public abstract still does not summarize the actual hosting architecture, uptime/SLA expectations, migration work, cybersecurity responsibilities, or content-update boundaries
The posting is classified under Goods / General Support Services, so the buyer may still lean toward a supplier already positioned for managed hosting operations
Because the category-page crawl was not repeatable from the automation runtime today, this item is carried forward from the official August 29 recheck rather than a fresh full-page recrawl
best_opportunities.recommended_next_action: Review the linked RFQ immediately, confirm whether Red PhilGEPS registration is acceptable, and verify the hosting stack, uptime/support SLA, migration obligations, security responsibilities, and whether website enhancement work is included.

best_opportunities.project: 2026-08-4390 Procurement of Website Development and Implementation Services
best_opportunities.why_fit: This is still a direct website-development procurement under a small-value route with a realistic budget and a 48-day delivery window, which keeps it close to AIStaff’s custom systems and implementation capabilities.
important_requirements: Official public abstract shows only one line item: Website Development and Implementation Services
Official public abstract shows delivery period: 48 days
Official public abstract lists contact person: Gerardo F. L. Micor, BAC Secretariat/PGADH-Provincial Budget Office, quezonbac@gmail.com, (042) 719-1130
Official public abstract says: Inquire at the Office of the Department of Education (DepEd) - Quezon for details
Public abstract does not clearly state the PhilGEPS membership level requirement, document checklist, or prior-experience threshold
risks_or_blockers: The public abstract remains unusually sparse and still does not describe the actual website scope, number of pages, integrations, hosting model, warranty terms, or acceptance criteria
The note to inquire with DepEd-Quezon still conflicts with the posting header that names Province of Quezon as procuring entity
This closes on August 31, 2026, so there is very little preparation time left if the RFQ packet is not already in hand
best_opportunities.recommended_next_action: Request the RFQ packet immediately, confirm whether Red PhilGEPS registration is acceptable, and ask which entity controls scope clarifications, submissions, hosting ownership, and post-launch support.

not_recommended.procuring_entity: Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources - RV
not_recommended.reason: This still reads as a bundled branded-license and subscription purchase. It is a reseller/license-supply opportunity, not a custom AI systems, managed support, or implementation engagement that fits AIStaff cleanly.

not_recommended.project: ESTABISHMENT OF ENHANCED TAX REVENUE ASSESSMENT AND COLLECTION SYSTEM (E-TRACS)
not_recommended.procuring_entity: Municipality of Del Gallego, Camarines Sur
not_recommended.reason: The public abstract points to an annual E-TRACS sustainability subscription under Limited Source Bidding, which looks incumbent-specific and product-tied rather than a realistic open custom-system opportunity for a new supplier.

not_recommended.project: Provision of Software and Application Development Services
not_recommended.reason: The service fit is real, but the public notice describes a global long-term OICT roster spanning enterprise applications, cloud, security, AI, data, managed services, and resource augmentation. That breadth is too large and enterprise-heavy for a small/new supplier first UN pursuit even though registration level is Basic.

This is attractive on paper, but the public notice explicitly wants a prime system integrator to procure, configure, implement, migrate data, integrate Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP and Microsoft 365, train users, and provide SLA-backed support. That is too enterprise-integrator-heavy for AIStaff’s current profile.

This is the closest direct chatbot fit in today’s UNGM scan, but it is Spanish-language, Mexico-specific, and likely favors suppliers that can deliver local-context financial-inclusion content and support. For AIStaff it is more of a stretch than a practical near-term target.

todays_recommendation.best_opportunity: RFQ no. 2026-08-28-006 Website Hosting and Technical Support Services for the Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (Ref 13217867) remains the best opportunity to pursue today because it is still the cleanest service-led fit and closes soon enough to justify immediate RFQ review.
documents_to_prepare: Notarized Omnibus Sworn Statement with proof of signatory authority
Latest 2025 annual income tax return and recent business tax returns
One-page capability sheet focused on website operations, implementation, support, automation, and integrations
Short hosting-and-support approach note covering uptime handling, backup responsibilities, migration, security, and support response process
clarifications_to_request: For CCP: whether Red PhilGEPS registration is acceptable for this small-value RFQ
For CCP: the exact hosting stack, traffic expectations, uptime/support SLA, backup responsibilities, and whether website enhancements are included
For Quezon: whether the project is a new build, redesign, migration, or implementation of an approved design
For Quezon: which entity controls the detailed requirements and submissions, Province of Quezon BAC or DepEd-Quezon
For both PhilGEPS opportunities: whether any prior government website or hosting experience is mandatory in the detailed RFQ packet

notes: PhilGEPS was checked through official public notice pages and tracked official notice links only. No login, CAPTCHA bypass, or restricted document access was attempted.
UNGM was checked through the official public UNGM search/notices pages using the repo’s live public scan script against current notices.
No genuinely suitable new opportunity surfaced today. The two PhilGEPS items carried in BEST OPPORTUNITIES are previously reported notices that now close within the next three days.

Tiwi Disaster AI (PhilGEPS Ref 13211679) was still visible as active in current public indexing, but no new material change was confirmed today and it does not meet the within-three-days carry-forward rule for this August 30 briefing.

Publicly visible UNGM attachments/links were referenced for screening only. For example, the UN Secretariat EOI page exposed a public EOI PDF link and the WMO notice exposed public tender-document links, but this run did not assume any hidden requirement beyond what was visible on the public notice pages.

The PhilGEPS category-page crawl was not fully repeatable from the automation runtime because direct fetches looped redirects. This report therefore uses a conservative PhilGEPS count and a targeted urgent-item recheck instead of claiming a full category crawl.
